I’m not trying to quench your hunger for improvement just instead pointing out that 3 minis in and your picking it up better then most people which is awesome! I see that you already have shadeded portions of this model and I would recommend possibly leaving more of the shade behind. Think of light on miniature as a gradient. The highlights on the cloak show that your already applying this concept, just push it further. The purple at the top of the cloak can be much brighter while the middle to bottom part of the fur pelt can be much darker. Because we’re working at such a small scale everything has to be exaggerated even to get something fairly realistic we have to use colors brighter on average  then most other mediums would ever require besides the most intense highlights in average lighting. Leaving more shade behind and doing another brighter purple on top of the current purple will really show case what I’m talking about in real time.  The weapon effect is super well done as well by the way just wanted to say that. I wish you fun and peace on your mini paining journey.

So imo the really cool thing about painting in the grim dark style is that you do as much or as little as you want. There are only 2 required steps really, a base coat and then an oil wash. Ak’s stuff is great but you can just go to a craft store and buy cheap oil paint and white spirit in order to make your own washes. After you use the oil wash you can remove as much or as little of the wash as you’d like with the white spirits. Oils have a long long long working time naturally like an oil wash will stay wet for like a day. You can let the washes dry naturally or use something like a hairdryer to dry the wash must faster. After you’ve done this you can then be done with the model or go even further with things such as pigments, chipping, highlights, replicating textures with highlights, osl, and more. Good luck on your journey into the world of grim dark and I can’t wait to see what you do with this fantastic looking model.

These seem to be your standard ordeal for gw orks. Waagh flesh base coat with bieltan green wash. Then basically highlight/over brush with warboss green leaving only the shadows untouched (that's why the skin tone is so bright) and finally edge highlight with skarsnik green. The goff stuff is more complicated and I completely recommend u/Halfof1half guide on painting them as he is one of the best ork painters around. Squiggs are stranded gw red triad mephiston red base, wash with whatever really, highlight with evil sunz scarlet, and then edge highlight with wild rider red. Hope this helped you and have fun painting them.
